title: Vibe coding, or engineering?
intro: Sort each behaviour: is this the disposable loop, or spec-driven discipline?

cards.text: Correcting the result by chatting until it looks right
The design decisions live only in a long chat history
"Make it green and big" as the entire requirement
Starting a fresh session means re-explaining everything
A version-controlled spec captures the what & why
A large UI overhaul is triggered by editing a few spec sentences
Success criteria and constraints are written before any code
A new agent picks up the project mid-stream and stays aligned

debrief: The tell is **where intent lives**. If it lives in a disposable dialogue, you're vibe coding: fast, unrepeatable, and compounding technical debt. If it lives in a maintained spec, you get the three SDD benefits — small edits steer large changes, no context decay across sessions or agents, and code that matches intent because the intent was written down first.
